problem.title: Design a 15,000 RPS Semantic & Prompt Caching Tier for Foundation Models
problem.tagline: Resolve >25% of LLM traffic in <15 ms p99 across 100M entries with zero cross-tenant bleed and O(1) epoch invalidation.
problem.purpose: Design a multi-tenant semantic and prompt caching tier that cuts foundation model inference spend while maintaining <15 ms p99 evaluation overhead and <0.5% hallucination drift.
problem.prompt: Design a Semantic & Prompt Caching Tier for a multi-tenant LLM gateway handling 5,000 RPS sustained (15,000 RPS peak), targeting >25% cache hit ratio, <15 ms p99 cache evaluation latency, and 100M cached prompt-response entries with strict tenant isolation and dynamic invalidation.

prerequisites.title: Dual-Tier Radix Prefix & HNSW Semantic Caching
prerequisites.summary: Understand how L1 exact prefix tries complement L2 SQ8 HNSW semantic vector search.

prerequisites.title: Little's Law & Tail Latency Budgets
prerequisites.summary: Know how to size ONNX embedding worker pools and enforce fail-open circuit breakers.

spark.summary: Combine <1 ms L1 Radix prefix hashing with 12 ONNX INT8 embedding workers, 8-shard SQ8 HNSW (110.7 GB DRAM), Zstd NVMe RocksDB (400 GB), and O(1) model-epoch invalidation.
spark.keyTakeaway: When designing a foundation model caching tier at 15,000 peak RPS and 100M entries, separate L1 Radix prefix matching from tenant-isolated L2 SQ8 HNSW lookup, guard hits with entity/negation checks, and fail open under 15 ms.
spark.byteSummary:
Sending 5,000–15,000 RPS of repetitive enterprise prompts directly to 70B+ foundation models burns GPU HBM bandwidth and inflates TTFT. A dedicated caching tier must evaluate both exact system-prompt prefixes (L1) and paraphrased user queries (L2) in under 15 ms p99.

The architecture hashes canonicalized 256-token prefixes in an in-memory Radix Trie (<1 ms) and routes L1 misses to 12 ONNX INT8 embedding workers (<=4 ms) feeding 8 sharded SQ8 HNSW nodes (110.7 GB DRAM at RF=2, <=6 ms) backed by 400 GB Zstd NVMe RocksDB.

Strict HMAC-SHA256 tenant salting + Roaring Bitmap pre-filtering prevent cross-tenant vector bleed, while O(1) model_epoch tags and a 5% async shadow drift monitor keep stale or hallucinated hits below 0.5%.

learningJourney.title: R & E · Requirements, Scale Targets & 100M Entry Sizing
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Establishes the <15 ms p99 latency budget and proves 100M entries fit in 110.7 GB DRAM + 400 GB NVMe.

explanation.foundation: Targets: 5,000 RPS sustained, 15,000 RPS peak, >25% combined hit ratio, <15 ms p99 evaluation overhead, 100M active entries.
explanation.core: Sizing 100M 384-d SQ8 vectors = 38.4 GB + 14.4 GB HNSW edges (M=16) + 2.56 GB L1 Radix = 55.36 GB × 2 (RF=2) = 110.7 GB DRAM across 8 shards. Zstd-compressed payloads (2 KB avg) = 400 GB NVMe.
explanation.deepDive: By Little's Law at 15,000 peak RPS and 12 ms p95 evaluation, L = 180 concurrent in-flight lookups. With 88% L1 miss rate (13,200 embeddings/sec), 12 ONNX INT8 workers (1,600 req/s each) provide N+2 headroom.

sectionDiagram.title: FP32 Unsharded vs. SQ8 Sharded DRAM + NVMe RocksDB

learningJourney.title: S & H · Storage Entities & 5-Tier Decoupled Architecture
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Separates hot vector graph traversal from compressed payload persistence and async write-back.

explanation.foundation: Edge Gateway normalizes prompts and derives tenant_hash = HMAC-SHA256(master_key, tenant_id). L1 Radix Trie checks exact matches and emits GPU KV-cache pod affinity hints.
explanation.core: L2 queries sharded SQ8 HNSW with a Roaring Bitmap tenant pre-filter, then fetches the Zstd payload from NVMe RocksDB.
explanation.deepDive: Cache misses stream directly from the Foundation Model Origin while publishing WriteBackEvents to Kafka for async PII scrubbing, deduplication, and HNSW + RocksDB commit.

learningJourney.title: A & D · RPC Contracts, Cosine Calibration & Slot Guard
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Formalizes typed lookup/invalidation RPCs and prevents false-positive semantic hits.

explanation.foundation: EvaluateCache accepts (tenant_id, model_id, model_epoch, system_prompt_hash, user_prompt, max_cosine_dist, deadline_ms) and returns hit_tier + cached_payload + kv_prefix_affinity.
explanation.core: Cosine distance calibration divides space into Safe (d < 0.08), Gray (0.08 <= d < 0.14), and Reject (d >= 0.14). An Entity/Negation Slot Guard enforces exact parity on numbers, dates, and negations.
explanation.deepDive: Concurrent identical misses coalesce via singleflight in the gateway so only one origin GPU call executes.

learningJourney.title: E · Technology Trade-Offs, Dynamic TTL & Epoch Invalidation
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Justifies HNSW SQ8 over DiskANN/IVF-PQ and RocksDB over Postgres/S3 under <15 ms p99.

explanation.foundation: HNSW SQ8 delivers 96.5% Recall@10 in 5.5 ms p99; DiskANN takes 18–25 ms on NVMe (violating SLA) and IVF-PQ distorts cosine distances near tau = 0.08.
explanation.core: Volatility-aware TTL assigns 7d to static docs, 1h to RAG knowledge, and 0s bypass to live data. Bumping model_epoch invalidates stale entries in O(1) without cluster-wide flushes.
explanation.deepDive: RocksDB compaction filters purge expired or old-epoch keys asynchronously during background SST merges.

learningJourney.title: D · Failure Modes, Circuit Breakers, Assumptions & Glossary
learningJourney.whyThisMatters: Ensures cache failures degrade cost efficiency only—never availability or tenant security.

explanation.foundation: Three circuit breakers govern safety: Latency Breaker (>12 ms p99 opens L2 bypass), Drift Breaker (5% shadow LLM Judge drift >1.5% tightens tau from 0.08 to 0.05), and Queue Shedding (worker depth >64).
explanation.core: Assumptions & Limitations: Assumes low-temperature (T <= 0.3) workloads and canonicalizable prompts; high-entropy creative generation or strict real-time feeds must set bypass_cache = true.
explanation.deepDive: Glossary: L1 Radix Trie, L2 SQ8 HNSW, Cosine Distance tau, Roaring Bitmap Pre-Filter, HMAC Tenant Salt, Model-Version Epoch, Entity/Negation Slot Guard, Singleflight Coalescing, Fail-Open Breaker, Shadow Drift Monitor.

decisionExercise.prompt: A deployment upgrades Llama-3.3-70B weights from v4.1 to v4.2 during peak 15,000 RPS traffic. How do you invalidate stale cached responses without crashing the GPU cluster?

options.label: Bump the global model_epoch from v4.1 to v4.2 in etcd/Redis so stale entries miss lazily
options.feedback: Correct—O(1) epoch tagging avoids a sudden 100% cache flush and lets RocksDB compact old entries gradually.

options.label: Delete all HNSW collections and rebuild from scratch
options.feedback: Deleting collections causes an immediate thundering herd on the origin GPUs.

steps.label: L1 Prefix Lookup
steps.detail: Check HMAC-salted XXH3-64 Radix Trie (<1 ms). Hit returns immediately or passes KV affinity hint.

steps.label: L2 Vector & Slot Gate
steps.detail: ONNX INT8 embeds user turn (4 ms); SQ8 HNSW + Roaring tenant filter + Slot Guard evaluate in <6 ms.

steps.label: Origin & Async Write-Back
steps.detail: Misses stream from LLM Origin while Kafka + PII Scrubber asynchronously commit new entries.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does the design use Roaring Bitmap pre-filtering in HNSW instead of post-filtering top-K results by tenant_id?

options.text: Post-filtering can return zero results for small tenants and leaks neighbor graph structure
options.feedback: Correct—if top-K neighbors belong to a large noisy tenant, post-filtering yields empty results and degrades recall.

options.text: Pre-filtering doubles the vector dimension from 384 to 768
options.feedback: Bitmaps filter node IDs without changing vector dimensions.
RocksDB only serves point reads after HNSW returns IDs.
Bitmaps restrict candidate nodes; cosine distance still ranks them.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Pre-filtering guarantees strict tenant isolation and preserves Recall@K even when one tenant dominates entry count.

knowledgeChecks.question: At 15,000 peak RPS with an 88% L1 miss rate and 1,600 prompts/sec per ONNX INT8 worker, how many workers are needed for N+2 redundancy?

options.feedback: A single worker saturates at 1,600 RPS.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why are prompt-response payloads stored in NVMe RocksDB rather than inside HNSW DRAM?

options.text: RocksDB computes cosine similarity faster than DRAM
options.feedback: HNSW in DRAM handles vector similarity; RocksDB handles key-value payloads.

options.text: Keeping 400 GB of Zstd payloads on NVMe avoids paying 10–15x DRAM cost for cold text bytes
options.feedback: Correct—only 384-d SQ8 vectors and graph edges need DRAM; payloads sit cheaply on NVMe.
HNSW stores SQ8 integers and node IDs.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Separating hot vector indexes (DRAM) from Zstd payloads (NVMe) optimizes cost per GB while keeping point reads <1 ms.

knowledgeChecks.question: What action does the Async Shadow Drift Monitor take when hallucination drift exceeds 1.5%?

options.feedback: Loosening tau increases false-positive hits and drift.

options.text: Tightens tau from 0.08 to 0.05 or trips the tenant L2 circuit breaker
options.feedback: Correct—tightening tau immediately raises semantic precision.
L1 exact matches have zero semantic drift.
Write-back continues for valid origin responses.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Tightening cosine threshold tau narrows the semantic acceptance radius to curb drift.

beginner.summary: Build an LLM cache with an exact prefix lookup tier and a vector similarity tier backed by fast SSD storage.
beginner.keyTakeaway: When scaling an AI cache, keep vector indexes in memory for speed and compressed text responses on NVMe SSDs for cost.
beginner.byteSummary: An LLM cache checks exact prompt prefixes first (<1 ms) and then searches similar questions in a vector index (<15 ms), falling back to the LLM on a miss.

intermediate.summary: Architect a 15K peak RPS dual-tier cache using L1 Radix Trie, ONNX INT8 workers, 8-shard SQ8 HNSW, and Zstd RocksDB.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: When designing a multi-tenant semantic cache, enforce tenant pre-filtering, entity/negation guards, and fail-open timeouts under 15 ms.
intermediate.byteSummary: 100M 384-d SQ8 vectors fit in 110.7 GB DRAM (RF=2) with 400 GB Zstd RocksDB on NVMe. Async Kafka write-back keeps streaming TTFT unblocked.

advanced.summary: Full Principal blueprint: Little's Law worker sizing, SQ8 HNSW Roaring Bitmap isolation, O(1) model_epoch invalidation, and closed-loop shadow drift breakers.
advanced.keyTakeaway: When operating a 100M-entry semantic cache at 15,000 peak RPS, bind HMAC tenant isolation, O(1) epoch tags, and async 5% shadow drift breakers with fail-open origin fallback.
advanced.byteSummary: Balances sub-15 ms p99 evaluation against <0.5% drift via calibrated tau=0.08, lexical slot guards, singleflight miss coalescing, and RocksDB compaction-filter TTL cleanup.
